evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) not on dialysis in primary care: detection, GFR/ACR classification, monitoring, referral, blood pressure and proteinuria treatment, SGLT2 inhibitors, cardiovascular protection and complications. Verified against NICE NG203; doses and contraindications from US FDA prescribing information. KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline and Saudi national CKD guidance were not reviewed for this version. Acute kidney injury is covered in its own topic.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national CKD guideline reviewed
Bicarbonate, phosphate binder, iron and ESA dosing — renal protocol

pathophysiology.summary: CKD is abnormal kidney structure or function present for more than 3 months — eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² and/or markers of damage such as albuminuria (ACR 3 mg/mmol or more), haematuria or structural abnormality. Risk of progression, AKI, cardiovascular events and death rises with lower GFR and higher ACR, and the two multiply (NICE).
keyMechanisms: Common causes: diabetic kidney disease and hypertension; also glomerulonephritis, polycystic kidney disease, obstruction, recurrent pyelonephritis, nephrotoxic drugs.
Nephron loss → hyperfiltration of remaining nephrons (raised glomerular pressure) → proteinuria, glomerulosclerosis and further loss — the target of RAS blockade and SGLT2 inhibition.
Albuminuria signals glomerular damage and predicts progression and cardiovascular risk.
Falling GFR causes retention of potassium, phosphate, acid and fluid; reduced erythropoietin (anaemia) and calcitriol (secondary hyperparathyroidism, bone disease).
CKD greatly increases cardiovascular risk — most patients die of CVD before needing dialysis.

symptoms: Usually asymptomatic until advanced — found on blood/urine testing.
Advanced: fatigue, itch, nausea, poor appetite, breathlessness, ankle swelling, nocturia.
physicalSigns: Uraemic signs in kidney failure: pericardial rub, asterixis.
redFlags: Potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more; severe acidosis, uraemia or fluid overload — urgent care
Sustained eGFR fall of 25% or more with category change within 12 months, or 15 mL/min/1.73 m² or more per year
ACR 70 mg/mmol or more (unless diabetic and already treated), or ACR above 30 with haematuria
Hypertension uncontrolled on 4 or more drugs; suspected renal artery stenosis or outflow obstruction
precipitants: Family history of kidney failure; polycystic kidney disease
Recurrent urinary tract infection, stones, obstruction

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Rapid creatinine rise; may be on CKD — monitor at least 3 years after AKI.
Creatinine-based eGFR unreliable; avoid meat 12 h before testing (NICE).

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Risk groups (diabetes, hypertension, CVD, structural disease, family history, after AKI, nephrotoxic drugs); confirm a new eGFR below 60 within 2 weeks
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: CKD needs abnormality for more than 3 months. Progression: sustained fall of 25% or more with category change, or 15 mL/min/1.73 m² per year.
ruleIn.normalValue: eGFR 90 or more (60–89 without other markers is not CKD)

references.title: NICE NG203: Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management

ruleIn.modalityTarget: With eGFR in all at risk; confirm 3–70 mg/mmol on an early-morning sample
ruleIn.expectedFinding: A1 below 3; A2 3–30; A3 above 30 mg/mmol. 70 or more = heavy proteinuria (no repeat needed).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Drives treatment and referral; use ACR, not reagent strips.

ruleIn.testName: Potassium and eGFR before and 1–2 weeks after starting or increasing ACE inhibitor/ARB
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Do not start if potassium above 5.0; stop if 6.0 or more. eGFR fall below 25% (or creatinine rise below 30%): continue and recheck.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Fall of 25% or more: look for other causes, then stop or reduce (NICE).

ruleIn.testName: Haemoglobin; ferritin and TSAT if anaemic
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Hb 110 g/L or less → assess anaemia of CKD.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Correct iron first; ESA via specialist.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: High phosphate, high PTH; bicarbonate below 20 mmol/L.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Phosphate binders, bicarbonate (G4–G5 with bicarbonate below 20).

clinicalManagement.title: Detect and classify
actions: Test eGFR and ACR in people at risk; confirm with repeat tests; classify by GFR (G1–G5) and ACR (A1–A3) categories.
Estimate 5-year kidney failure risk with the 4-variable Kidney Failure Risk Equation.
Agree monitoring frequency by GFR/ACR category and rate of change (NICE Table 2).

clinicalManagement.title: Blood pressure
actions: ACR below 70 mg/mmol: clinic BP below 140/90 (systolic target 120–139).
Hypertension with ACR above 30 mg/mmol: ACE inhibitor or ARB titrated to highest tolerated licensed dose; otherwise treat per hypertension guideline.

clinicalManagement.title: Proteinuria and progression
actions: Diabetes with ACR 3 mg/mmol or more: ACE inhibitor or ARB at the highest tolerated dose.
No diabetes, ACR 70 or more: refer to nephrology and start ACE inhibitor or ARB; ACR 30–70: monitor and discuss with nephrology if worsening.
SGLT2 inhibitor as add-on (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) per NICE TAs; finerenone for CKD 3–4 with type 2 diabetes and ACR 3 or more (TA877).
Never combine RAS antagonists (ACE inhibitor + ARB).

clinicalManagement.title: Cardiovascular protection
actions: Atorvastatin 20 mg for primary or secondary prevention; increase if target not met and eGFR 30 or more (see Dyslipidaemia topic).
Antiplatelet for secondary prevention — higher bleeding risk.

clinicalManagement.title: Complications (G3b–G5)
actions: Anaemia: assess when Hb 110 g/L or less; iron then ESA (specialist).
Metabolic acidosis: consider oral sodium bicarbonate if eGFR below 30 and bicarbonate below 20 mmol/L (dose per local renal protocol).
Phosphate: dietary advice, then calcium acetate (or sevelamer) per specialist.
Avoid long-term NSAIDs; review renally cleared drugs and sick-day rules (pause ACE inhibitor/ARB, SGLT2 inhibitor, metformin, diuretics during dehydrating illness).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
actions: KFRE 5-year risk above 5%; ACR 70 or more (unless diabetic and treated); ACR above 30 with haematuria; rapid eGFR decline; uncontrolled BP on 4 drugs; genetic causes; renal artery stenosis (NICE 1.5.5).

learningObjectives: Detect, classify and manage chronic kidney disease to slow progression and reduce cardiovascular risk.

keyPoints: Classify by GFR and ACR — both matter.
ACE inhibitor or ARB for diabetes with ACR 3+, or ACR above 30 with hypertension.
Add an SGLT2 inhibitor; never combine ACE inhibitor and ARB.
Check potassium and eGFR 1–2 weeks after RAS changes.
Atorvastatin 20 mg for all with CKD.
pitfalls: Using dipstick protein instead of ACR.
Stopping RAS blockers for a small expected eGFR dip.
Missing rapid progression by not trending eGFR.

patientEducation: What CKD and the GFR/ACR numbers mean.
Sick-day rules for ACE inhibitor/ARB, SGLT2 inhibitor, metformin, diuretics.
Avoid over-the-counter NSAIDs and herbal remedies.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking; regular exercise; healthy weight.
Dietary advice tailored to stage (potassium, phosphate) from a renal dietitian.
mdtReferrals: Urology for outflow obstruction or haematuria work-up.
Dietitian for potassium/phosphate advice in advanced CKD.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: eGFR and ACR at a frequency set by GFR/ACR category (at least annually; more often in G3b–G5 or A3), plus potassium after any RAS-blocker change; BP at every review.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: eGFR below 60 and/or ACR 3 mg/mmol or more (or other markers) for more than 3 months
KFRE above 5% at 5 years; ACR 70 or more; rapid decline

regimens.indication: CKD with diabetes and ACR 3 or more, or hypertension with ACR above 30
regimens.dose: 2.5 mg (start; range up to 20 mg daily per label)
regimens.frequency: Once daily; titrate to highest tolerated licensed dose
adjustments: Do not start if potassium above 5.0
Check potassium and eGFR 1–2 weeks after each change

regimens.frequency: Once daily; increase to 100 mg by BP response
adjustments: Same potassium/eGFR monitoring as ACE inhibitors

regimens.indication: Add-on to optimised care for CKD (NICE TA1075)
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with eGFR 25 or more at initiation
regimens.duration: Long term (continue if eGFR later falls below 25 until dialysis per label)
adjustments: Do not initiate if eGFR below 25 (label)
Pause during acute illness/fasting; withhold 3 days before surgery
monitoring: eGFR (expect small initial dip), volume status, genital infection

medicationPlan.note: Indications are from NICE NG203/NG238; doses and contraindications from US FDA labels. Sodium bicarbonate, phosphate binders, iron and ESA doses per local renal protocol. Check SFDA registration, formulary and availability.
